status: Curling and nozzle pickup reported; no completed-part acceptance

observations.observation: At about layer 28, roughly 1 mm of the outside underside curled upward on the left as viewed from the printer door. The next layers pressed it down and it sprang back; around layer 31 a glob was pulled off and carried elsewhere.
The left growing lip is visibly raised. The base appears seated in this view; the photo does not establish adhesion over the whole foot.

observations.quote: Haha, just to test, I dropped part fan from 100 to 50 just now and like instantly we got more curl on that left edge and then the right edge curled too.

observations.source: Printer telemetry after user reported bed cleared

interpretation: The runtime fan reduction worsened the observed curl on this print. The archived 100% fan baseline had already shown left-edge curl.
The observed left lip is not at the seam or an extrusion restart. Around the reported onset it has about 82% nominal previous-layer bead overlap.
Geometric bead overlap does not establish resistance to thermal or mechanical deformation.

At the reported onset, the left underside is about 45 degrees from the bed and the right about 66 degrees. Nominal local bead overlap is approximately 82% left and 92% right. This asymmetry is consistent with left-first curling but does not establish its cause.
scope: Print-process observations only; socket fit, sealing, retention and lifetime remain unmeasured.
